# Probability and Statistical Models

- [From a sampling model to a likelihood](#from-a-sampling-model-to-a-likelihood)
- [Prior information and prior prediction](#prior-information-and-prior-prediction)

## From a sampling model to a likelihood

- Conditional probability, Bayes' rule, and the role of a statistical model
- Sampling distribution versus likelihood; exchangeability and conditional independence

Agresti 1.1–1.3 and selected 1.7 material

## Prior information and prior prediction

- Proper, weakly informative, and improper priors
- Conjugacy as a transparent example; prior prediction with proper priors
- Check posterior propriety when using an improper prior

Agresti 1.3 and 1.7

# Posterior Inference and Prediction

- [The posterior and posterior summaries](#the-posterior-and-posterior-summaries)
- [Intervals, comparisons, and predictions](#intervals-comparisons-and-predictions)

## The posterior and posterior summaries

- Normalizing a posterior; mean, median, and mode
- Loss, risk, and posterior decisions; shrinkage as a preview

Agresti 1.4

## Intervals, comparisons, and predictions

- Credible and HPD intervals; confidence-interval distinctions
- Posterior comparisons and the posterior predictive distribution

Agresti 1.5–1.6

# Assumptions and Interpretation

- [Check what the prior and model imply](#check-what-the-prior-and-model-imply)
- [Planned Python demonstration](#planned-python-demonstration)

## Check what the prior and model imply

- Prior sensitivity, the likelihood principle, and model limitations
- Link prior prediction, posterior prediction, and substantive interpretation

Agresti 1.7–1.8

## Planned Python demonstration

- A small discrete parameter grid: normalize, summarize, and predict
- Compare two priors and explain why the answers differ

No companion notebook released yet
